questions.explanation: A path on 6 vertices connects them in a single chain with n-1 edges, giving 5. Adding more edges would create a branch or cycle, which a path does not have.
questions.hint: A path on n vertices has n minus 1 edges.

questions.learningObjective: Solve an exam-level problem in discrete mathematics from first principles.
questions.stem: How many edges does the complete graph K6 have? Report the result, using only the information above.
questions.explanation: K6 has one undirected edge per pair of vertices, so C(6,2)=15 edges. Ordered pairs would double the count because edge {u,v} equals {v,u}.
questions.hint: Count unordered pairs of vertices.

questions.learningObjective: Solve an exam-level problem in discrete mathematics from first principles.
questions.stem: Read 7 and undefined first: how many edges does the complete bipartite graph K(7,7) have? Give the exact answer, using only the information above.
questions.explanation: In K(7,7) every vertex of one part joins every vertex of the other, giving 7*7=49 edges. There are no edges inside a part.
questions.hint: Multiply the sizes of the two parts.
